status.summary: Former UFC middleweight and two-time light heavyweight champion. He vacated the light heavyweight belt to move up and lost his heavyweight debut to Ciryl Gane for the interim heavyweight title at UFC Freedom 250 on the White House South Lawn (Jun 14, 2026, TKO R2 1:27; Gane out-landed him 54-12). He is booked against Sergei Pavlovich in a five-round heavyweight co-main event at UFC 335 (Dec 12, 2026, T-Mobile Arena, Las Vegas), announced by Dana White on the UFC 332 broadcast (Oct 3, 2026). Pro record 13-4 per post-fight reports.
status.next_fight: Sergei Pavlovich, UFC 335, Dec 12, 2026, T-Mobile Arena, Las Vegas (heavyweight, 5 rounds, co-main event)

style.summary: A former Glory kickboxing champion at middleweight and light heavyweight who walks opponents down behind a high guard, chops the lead leg and ends fights with one shot: 8 of his 10 UFC wins are KO/TKO, including a left head kick and a flying knee. He rarely wrestles; his risk is being pinned to the fence by a control fighter, as in the first Ankalaev fight, or out-sped by a bigger man, as against Gane.

moves.notes: Each group (head, body, leg) sums to 1; the engine's target split picks the group. From the decayed sums in fighters.json his significant attempts go 60% head, 17% body, 22% legs, and his landed strikes 47% head, 22% body, 30% legs (leg accuracy 0.82, body 0.77, head 0.47), so the legs are his surest target. In the head group the left hook gets the top weight because his finishes of Hill (UFC 300) and Rountree (UFC 307) were single punches at distance and it is his best-known weapon; head kick 0.10 reflects the UFC 303 KO of Prochazka and his kickboxing base. Leg kicks lean to the outside rear-leg low kick and calf (48/55 legs landed vs Ankalaev at UFC 313; 26/36 vs Adesanya at UFC 287). Knee 0.15 covers the flying knee (UFC 268) and clinch knees; elbow 0.20 covers ground elbows (UFC 295, UFC 320). No spinning attacks appear in his UFC finishes. Sources: data/derived/fighters.json; ufcstats per-fight totals in data/raw.

Takedown defense 86% decayed (opponents about 2.3 of 16.7) and 80% career, but opponents' control time is 170 s per 15 min decayed, mostly cage clinch control by Ankalaev (342 s at UFC 313) and Adesanya (394 s at UFC 281).
Only one of his 13 UFC fights was at heavyweight (the Gane loss). His rates come from 185 and 205 lb fights, so heavyweight inputs should lean on the division prior.
Against Gane he landed 12 of 33 significant strikes, 8 of them leg kicks, and absorbed 54 (39 to the head).
